negative_findings.description: No public vendor case study, reference page or go-live press release was found naming the core-banking platform of any Montenegrin bank (CKB, Hipotekarna, NLB Podgorica, Erste ME, Addiko ME, Lovćen, Prva banka, Universal Capital, Adriatic, Ziraat ME).
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches across generic core-banking vendor queries, bank-specific queries and named-vendor queries (Temenos, Oracle FLEXCUBE, Backbase, Diebold Nixdorf, NCR) returned zero ME core-banking references. Only ancillary systems (security, SoftPOS, e-banking, CRM, HR, data centre) surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The core-banking layer is the highest-value procurement signal and it is invisible on the vendor side for ME. Coverage of this workstream must therefore lean on group-level parent disclosures (OTP, NLB, Erste, Addiko) and on bank T&C/app metadata fingerprints rather than vendor marketing.

negative_findings.description: No AML / financial-crime-compliance vendor was found publicly naming a Montenegrin bank as a customer.
negative_findings.result_summary: English-language searches on AML vendor + Montenegro returned only generic vendor-ranking listicles; no case study, press release or reference page named an ME institution.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: AML tooling is a mandated spend driven by MONEYVAL/EU-accession pressure, so the absence of vendor-side traces means this segment must be tracked via regulator (CBCG, Uprava za sprječavanje pranja novca) publications and bank annual reports instead of supplier marketing.

negative_findings.description: Local-language (sr/cnr) queries for AML vendor references were not productive because no ME-specific local vocabulary for AML product procurement surfaced in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local terms attempted for other subtopics (dobavljač, referenca, implementacija, saopštenje, ugovor, rješenje) worked well for ATM/POS, e-banking and integrator queries but the AML sweep was effectively English-only.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Per the mandate, English-only coverage is a defect. A follow-up pass must run terms such as 'sprječavanje pranja novca', 'softver za usklađenost', 'monitoring transakcija', 'sankcione liste' against ME vendor and bank sites.

negative_findings.description: The Logate corporate URL (logate.com) was inferred from company identity rather than confirmed in a search result; the confirmed trace was a third-party profile on itkonekt.com.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bank references for Logate (contact centre at Lovćen banka and CKB) appear in secondary Montenegrin sources, not yet confirmed on a vendor-owned page in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The vendor-owned reference page is the higher-credibility artefact and must be located and verified before the Lovćen/CKB contact-centre attribution is treated as established fact.

negative_findings.description: The available web search is US-biased and returned Wikipedia/bank-directory noise for many Montenegrin queries instead of vendor pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: Several sr-language queries returned generic bank profiles (thebanks.eu, Wikipedia, nomadcapitalist) rather than vendor references, indicating index thinness for the .me domain space.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Vendor-side discovery for ME likely requires site-scoped crawling (site:printecgroup.com, site:payten.com, site:asee.* plus each .me vendor domain) rather than open-web querying; this changes the collection design for this cell.

coverage_gaps.description: Card personalisation, card issuing/processing bureaus and switch vendors serving ME (beyond Payten/Bankart) are unmapped — e.g. who processes for Hipotekarna, Prva banka, Universal Capital, Adriatic and Ziraat ME.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run site-scoped sweeps of regional processors and issuers (Bankart, Payten/ASEE, Monri, Nets/Nexi, Halcom, Multicard/Multisoft, Intesa's regional hub) plus card T&C PDFs of each ME bank which frequently name the processor.

coverage_gaps.description: No site-scoped crawl was performed on the vendor domains identified (payten.com, printecgroup.com, see.asseco.com, halcom.com, bankart.si, plus ME integrators), so their full ME reference inventories remain unenumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a standing crawler over the ~15 identified vendor domains with a Montenegro/ME-bank-name keyword filter, run monthly, diffing new pages.

coverage_gaps.description: Montenegrin-specific orthography and alias variants were only partially exercised (cnr vs sr; 'rješenje' vs 'rešenje'; 'sprječavanje' vs 'sprečavanje'; Latin vs Cyrillic; CKB/Crnogorska komercijalna banka/OTP; NLB Banka Podgorica/NLB Banka Crna Gora/Montenegrobanka).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Compile a formal ME glossary with ijekavian/ekavian pairs, bank aliases and legacy names (Podgorička banka, Montenegrobanka, Societe Generale banka Montenegro → OTP/CKB) and re-run every query set in both variants.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor-side traces embedded in technical artefacts (mobile app package namespaces, SDK strings, e-banking login page footers, TLS certificate SANs, DNS/MX records of ME bank domains) were identified conceptually but not systematically collected.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a deterministic fingerprinting pass over all ME bank web/mobile properties to attribute channel vendors where marketing evidence is absent.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor-side evidence in parent-group reporting (OTP Group for CKB, NLB Group for NLB Podgorica, Erste Group, Addiko Group, Ziraat) was not sampled in this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Cross-link with the group-IR workstream: group annual reports and digital-transformation updates often name platform vendors that ME subsidiaries then inherit.

brief: Montenegro's vendor-side pointer landscape is thin but real, and it is concentrated in the ASEE/Payten orbit: Payten's news feed carries a named SoftPOS go-live at Hipotekarna banka, MoneyGet operates an ME ATM network, and E-mon Podgorica plus bank T&C PDFs (e.g. Ziraat ME) attribute the e-banking stack to Asseco SEE. Beyond that, the traces are ancillary rather than core — Qualys on CKB for security, Agilcon/Salesforce and Gecko HRM on Lovćen banka, One Crna Gora on Hipotekarna's data centre, and local integrators Logate, Čikom and Softing publishing bank-facing references. No public vendor reference of any kind names the core-banking platform of a Montenegrin bank, and no AML vendor names an ME client, so those layers must be reached indirectly via parent-group IR, regulator publications, and technical fingerprints (app package namespaces, T&C PDFs, login-page footers). The practical collection design for this cell is a site-scoped monthly crawl of roughly fifteen vendor domains with an ME-bank-name filter, rather than open-web querying, which returns directory noise for the .me space.
